verdict: Booking grew revenue 16% to $5.5B on $53.8B of gross bookings, and net income more than tripled to $1.1B — mostly because a $333M currency gain replaced a year-ago loss, while travel demand held up despite the Middle East conflict.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was $5.5B, or about +10% on a constant-currency basis

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Up 239% from $0.40 a year ago — per-share figures reflect the 25-for-1 stock split on April 2, 2026

kpis.label: Gross bookings
kpis.note: Up 15% from a year ago; room nights rose 6% to 338 million

kpis.label: Adjusted EPS
kpis.note: Adjusted net income rose 10% to $902M and adjusted EBITDA rose 19% to $1,290M

segments.name: Merchant revenues
segments.note: Booking collects the traveler's money itself and pays the hotel or airline — up 27% as Booking.com keeps shifting to this model

segments.name: Agency revenues
segments.note: Hotels and other providers pay Booking a commission and collect the traveler's money themselves — down 2% in the shift to merchant

segments.name: Advertising and other revenues
segments.note: Advertising on Booking's sites and OpenTable restaurant revenue — up 9%

opex.name: Marketing expenses
opex.note: Ads and partner marketing to bring in travelers — 3.8% of gross bookings, the same share as a year ago

opex.name: Sales and other expenses
opex.note: Payment processing for merchant bookings and customer-service costs

opex.name: Personnel
opex.note: Pay for the company's staff, including $141M of stock-based pay

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company — reduced this quarter by an $89M litigation-settlement gain

opex.name: Information technology
opex.note: Cloud, software and generative AI costs

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Wear and tear on buildings, equipment and software

opex.name: Transformation costs
opex.note: Costs of the company's transformation program

takeaways.title: Merchant is now the engine
takeaways.text: Merchant revenue rose 27% to $3.7B as Booking collects more travelers' payments itself, while agency revenue fell 2% to $1.5B — the ongoing shift from agency to merchant at Booking.com.

takeaways.title: Demand held up despite the conflict
takeaways.text: Room nights rose 6% to 338 million and gross bookings rose 15% to $53.8B, even though management estimates the Middle East conflict cut room-night and bookings growth by about 2 points. Alternative-accommodation room nights at Booking.com rose 5.5%.

takeaways.title: A currency swing flattered profit
takeaways.text: A $333M foreign-currency gain on remeasuring euro-denominated debt — versus a $437M loss a year ago — is the main reason GAAP net income jumped 225%, while adjusted net income rose a steadier 10% to $902M.

oneTimers: Foreign currency: a $333M gain on the remeasurement of euro-denominated debt and related derivatives, versus a $437M loss in Q1 2025; equity securities lost $107M in the quarter.
Booking received an $89M benefit from settling litigation in which it was a plaintiff, recorded as a reduction of general and administrative expenses.
Transformation costs were $25M in the quarter.

Stock split: Booking completed a 25-for-1 stock split on April 2, 2026, and all share and per-share figures in the filings are retroactively adjusted. The company also repurchased $3.6B of stock in the quarter, with $18.2B of authorization remaining.
otherDetail: Net other income was $128M: interest expense of -$253M, interest and dividend income of +$187M, and other income of +$194M. That $194M was a $333M foreign-currency gain on euro-debt remeasurement, less $107M of net losses on equity securities and $32M of other net items.
footerNote: Booking Holdings reports no cost of revenue — every cost is an operating expense, so gross profit equals revenue.
